name: Bright Aqua
lede: Bright Aqua is a vivid, near-neon aqua: the modifier "bright" on top of the base color, close enough to [[turquoise]] that several sources record the two as the same cluster.

sections.title: Three sources, one shade
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd survey, Wikipedia's color list, and a 1927 RAL paint standard all converge on essentially this hue, within about a CIEDE2000 unit of each other, close enough that our library records them as a near-duplicate it calls Turquoise Blue [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary places it in block 159, described as a vivid, light bluish green [2].

The name itself is plain modifier grammar, "bright" plus [[aqua]], and its closest learnable word in our library is Aqua itself, about 5 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. Siblings in the family are [[turquoise]], [[teal]], and [[mint]], all in the blue-green range this color sits at the saturated edge of [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this near-neon aqua covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. A color this bright and this light at once is outside the range historical pigments reach once mixed, applied, and aged under varnish [3].
